16133               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
16134               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
16135               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
16136               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
16137               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
16138               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
16139               	;
16140               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
16141               	; 	'
16142               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
16143               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
16144               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
16145               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
16146               	; 	'
16147               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
16148               	; 	'
16149               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
16150               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
16151               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
16152               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
16153               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
16154               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
16155               	; 	'
16156               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
16157               	; 	'
16158               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
16159               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
16160               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
16161               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
16162               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
16163               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
16164               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
16165               	; 	'
16166               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
16167               	; 	'
16168               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
16169               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
16170               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
16171               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
16172               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
16173               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
16174               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
16175               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
16176               	; 	'
16177               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
16178               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
16179               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
16180               	; 	'
16181               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
16182               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
16183               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
16184               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
16185               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
16186               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
16187               	; 	'
16188               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
16189               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
16190               	; 	'
16191               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
16192               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
16193               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
16194               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
16195               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
16196               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
16197               	; 	'
16198               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
16199               	; 	'
16200               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
16201               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the

16405               	;
16406               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
16407               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
16408               	; 	'
16409               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
16410               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
16411               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
16412               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
16413               	; 	'
16414               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
16415               	; 	'
16416               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
16417               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
16418               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
16419               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
16420               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
16421               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
16422               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
16423               	; 	'
16424               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
16425               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
16426               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
16427               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
16428               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
16429               	; 	'
16430               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
16431               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
16432               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
16433               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
16434               	; 	#if TI994A
16435               	; 	BANK 2
16436      01EC     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

16574               	;
16575               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($B4 = black ink on dark blue).
16576               	; 	'
16577               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
16578               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
16579               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
16580               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
16581               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
16582               	; 	'
16583               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
16584               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
16585               	;
16586               	; font_col:
16587               cvb_FONT_COL

16910               	; 	' AND THE TITLE'S DISPLAY LIST, for the same reason as the font: walked
16911               	; 	' once by title_draw, at boot and on a return to the title, and never
16912               	; 	' during play. title_draw selects bank 2 around its walk.
16913               	; 	'
16914               	; 	' ITS MESSAGE BOXES DID NOT COME WITH IT. They are the same format and
16915               	; 	' were in the same generated file, which is what made this worth doing
16916               	; 	' carefully: they are walked when a ROUND ENDS, mid-game, so on bank 2
16917               	; 	' they would have returned bytes from the wrong page at the moment a life
16918               	; 	' is lost -- and with no error at build or run time. gentitle.py now
16919               	; 	' writes them to title.bas below, which stays in bank 1.
16920               	; 	INCLUDE "titledl.bas"
16921               	; 	' ==================================================
16922               	; 	' THE TITLE SCREEN, AS A DISPLAY LIST
16923               	; 	' Generated by assets/gentitle.py -- do not edit here.
16924               	; 	'
16925               	; 	' row, col, length, then `length` bytes; 255 ends.
16926               	; 	' Walked by title_draw only.
16927               	; 	'
16928               	; 	' LIVES IN BANK 2, with the fonts, because it is read ONCE
16929               	; 	' -- at boot and on a return to the title. title_draw
16930               	; 	' selects bank 2 around its walk and restores bank 1.
16931               	; 	' The message boxes in title.bas are the same format and
16932               	; 	' CANNOT come with it: they are read when a round ends.
16933               	; 	' ==================================================
16934               	;

17163               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
17164               	; 	'
17165               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
17166               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
17167               	; 	' being small sprites.
17168               	; 	'
17169               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
17170               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
17171               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
17172               	; 	'
17173               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
17174               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
17175               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
17176               	;
17177               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/the four merged run bodies/duck hat/face/body, then the same LEFT (+36). The run bodies carry tunic AND legs, so a frame is one sprite. Patterns 0..68

18418               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
18419               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
18420               	; 	'
18421               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
18422               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
18423               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
18424               	; 	'
18425               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
18426               	; 	' blit is
18427               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
18428               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
18429               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
18430               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
18431               	; 	'
18432               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
18433               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
18434               	; 	'
18435               	; 	' template ids:
18436               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
18437               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
18438               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
18439               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
18440               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
18441               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
18442               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
18443               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
18444               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
18445               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
18446               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
18447               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
18448               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
18449               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
18450               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
18451               	;
18452               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
18453               cvb_STOR_TPL

19068               	;
19069               	; 	' THE SKYLINE'S LAST BAND WITHOUT ITS YELLOW, high nibble ink, low nibble
19070               	; 	' paper, one byte a scan line -- the same shape genart emits into
19071               	; 	' store_col. SKY2 is white-on-9 throughout instead of turning to paper 10
19072               	; 	' at row 4; BLDGL holds its blue one row longer and then meets its own
19073               	; 	' grey wall. Both are the generated bytes with 10 replaced by 9 and
19074               	; 	' nothing else changed. See setup_rest.
19075               	; #if NES
19076               	; nes_sky2c:
19077               	; 	DATA BYTE $F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9
19078               	; nes_bldlc:
19079               	; 	DATA BYTE $B9,$B9,$B9,$B9,$B9,$BE,$BE,$BE
19080               	; #endif
19081               	;
19082               	; 	' THE IN-GAME FONT'S COLOUR, one byte a scan line and eight a character for
19083               	; 	' all 59 of them. $B4 is light yellow on dark blue -- ink index 3, paper index 1 --
19084               	; 	' and which colours those are is then the attribute table's business, per
19085               	; 	' region: dark blue behind the HUD, the store's green behind a message box.
19086               	; 	'
19087               	; 	' 472 bytes of one repeated value. That reads like waste and is the cheap
19088               	; 	' option: ROM is three budgets here and this is not the scarce one, while
19089               	; 	' the alternative is a second font (impossible -- only eleven free codes)
19090               	; 	' or a new uploader parameter (no RAM -- two bytes left).

19092               	; nes_fcol:

19094               	; 	DATA BYTE $B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4
